reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that real-time markets do not fully process public information instantaneously. The benchmark-relative updating framework defines Δp = βΔq + γGap + η, where β ≠ 1 implies inefficiency. The updating gap Gap = Δq − Δp becomes a predictive signal for future drift. This is modeled through a drift regression: Gap predicts (p_{i,t+h} - p_it) over horizons h = 1 to 15 minutes. Liquidity and salience interact to gate the weight applied to market prices versus internal models. In GSE, this manifests as a dynamic state transition engine using weighted price signals. In GSI, it enables Bayesian calibration of predictive intervals. The failure mode occurs when β is not significantly different from 1, indicating full efficiency, which contradicts empirical findings. The model assumes exogeneity of signals and clustered standard errors. The breakdown regime is defined by thresholds such as |Δq| ≥ 0.0025 for directional underreaction. The drift prediction signal is robust across subsamples and holds even in clutch situations where β ≈ 0.51. The framework also accounts for microstructure effects like stale quotes and narrow spreads.
